turns.answer:
A small portable power station can keep your Wi-Fi router and modem running for 5–20+ hours during a power outage, depending on the battery capacity and how much electricity your equipment uses.

For most homes, I recommend a LiFePO₄ power station with 250–300Wh capacity. It's compact, quiet, rechargeable, and typically provides enough backup for an overnight outage.

How long will your Wi-Fi stay on?

A typical home setup uses:

Wi-Fi router: 8–15 watts

Cable modem or fiber ONT: 5–15 watts

Combined: approximately 15–30 watts

Important: keeping Wi-Fi connected without interruption

If you want the router and modem to stay on automatically when the power goes out, choose a model with UPS/EPS passthrough functionality, not just a battery with outlets. Test the transfer, since some networking equipment may reboot during switching.

Also, your internet provider's network must remain operational during the outage.
